description: FundKit service health: RED metrics for the HTTP and gRPC surfaces, the Kafka event pipeline, and Go runtime vitals. Engineered by Dhanush C N.

panels.title: Fleet overview — the four golden signals

panels.description: Every HTTP request served across the selected services. This is the RATE half of RED.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Server-side failures as a share of all traffic. Expressed as a ratio so a quiet service and a busy one are judged at the same sensitivity. clamp_min keeps the panel at 0 instead of NaN when there is no traffic at all.
panels.title: Error ratio (5xx)

panels.description: Computed from the histogram buckets at query time. Aggregating buckets first and taking the quantile second is the only way to get a fleet-wide p99 that means anything — averaging per-replica quantiles does not.
panels.title: p99 latency

panels.description: Messages the notification worker is behind the head of the topic. The one number that tells you whether the asynchronous half of the system is keeping up.
panels.title: Kafka consumer lag

panels.description: RPS per service. $__rate_interval adapts the window to the panel's resolution, so the shape stays honest when you zoom.
panels.title: Request throughput by service

panels.description: 4xx and 5xx are plotted separately on purpose: 5xx is the service failing, 4xx is callers being rejected. A 429 spike here is the gateway's rate limiter working, not an outage.
panels.title: Error ratio by service

panels.description: by (le, job) is not optional — histogram_quantile needs the le dimension intact after aggregation. Drop it and the query returns nothing.
panels.title: Latency percentiles

panels.description: Saturation. This climbs before latency does: when concurrency rises while throughput stays flat, requests are queueing on something downstream.
panels.title: Requests in flight

panels.description: Route templates, never raw paths — /orders/:id rather than /orders/9f3c…, so an order id can never become a time series of its own.
panels.title: Busiest routes

panels.description: The code label is where gRPC pays off: NotFound and DeadlineExceeded look identical at the transport layer and mean completely different things.
panels.title: RPC status codes

panels.description: Read these two lines together. Consumption below production is where backlog comes from; the lag panel beside this one is the integral of the gap.
panels.title: Publish vs consume rate

panels.description: Read at scrape time from the reader's own broker-sourced statistics, not polled and cached, so a dead reader stops reporting instead of freezing on its last value.
panels.title: Consumer lag

panels.description: Consume-side timing covers decode, handling and offset commit. Publish timing includes the RequireAll acknowledgement wait, so it moves the moment a broker replica falls out of the ISR.
panels.title: Event processing latency

panels.description: Three different failures. A publish error means the outbox is filling up. A handler error means the offset did not move and the message will be redelivered. A drop means the message was unparseable, was committed anyway, and is gone.
panels.title: Failed and dropped events

panels.description: A monotonic climb here is a goroutine leak, usually a missing context cancellation.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: 1.0 means one core fully busy. Compare against the CPU limit in k8s/*.yaml before blaming the code.
panels.title: CPU seconds per second
